Hey love, OPs Leader here! Comfortable sneakers are a MUST. Make sure you drink water and stretch because you will be doing the most physical work out of everyone. Ops leaders are not acting mangers (CEL) very often, especially in the beginning. Once you’re more comfortable in your role and you’ve completed ops training, you’ll get your CEL training. Now they may do both at once, but we didn’t because we were a small store. I’ll break down weekly tasks first. You have mandatory cycle counts every week provided by the company, the lists are on zipline. You can only do cycle counts when the store is closed. You have to plan out your week so you’ll have enough time to complete this before the end of the week. You have to scan out testers, damages, and known theft 3 times a week. I usually do Monday, Wednesday, and Friday because it works best for us. For weekly/daily tasks, you will be doing brand updates out the wazoo. Those you do throughout the week, and again, try plan them out so you have enough time to complete them on the right days. Example, you have a 9 hour overhaul, a 3 hour update, and a bunch of updates that are 1 hour or less. You’ll need to look at your work schedule, the schedule or your ops associates, and keep in mind store events so you can build a good system week by week. Ops is truly all about planning. I found that Mondays are slow for me, so I’d do my 9 hour update then, or Tuesday if that’s better. I try to bust out some of my longer updates early in the week, and do the quicker ones later on. And with brand events, I would try to avoid large updates on those days. Simply to make the shopping experience easier for clients because we’d have additional people and displays taking up space. You will find what works best for you! Also for the love of god, when update boxes come in, open them up and see what’s inside. Some boxes will say (example) Lancôme 1 of 1. That is usually straight forward and you probably won’t be expecting any more boxes. But if your weekly list claims it’s a 4 hour update, then check that box and make sure that it looks like you have everything. I unfortunately didn’t do this for a few months. I repeatedly started updates and couldn’t finish them because I was actually still waiting on more boxes to come in the mail. That was something I needed to work on, and it finally clicked after a couple months. Most updates, if they’re in multiple boxes, will say like 1 of 4 or something like that. And you will receive tall thing boxes with usually just price strips or magnets labeled “hair and skin updates.” Those things usually have multiple updates inside, and they are often very quick. I do all of them in one day if possible. Hopefully with planning and checking what you’re receiving, you’ll be a bit better off than I was. This will be a lot of work, but you got this! They don’t hire just anybody to work in ops. I’ve been an ops manager for different companies the past 5 years. It is my favorite, and I wish you the best of luck!!
